text:
noah: hey team, day 1 sync done. i'm on a company laptop (Win11) and connected to the split-tunnel VPN. i can't reach internal grafana at grafana.internal.redwood. browser just times out. i can ssh to bastion though. any short fixes?

mira: welcome noah! does `nslookup grafana.internal.redwood` on your laptop return anything? which client are you using (WireGuard/Tailscale/custom)?

noah: using the enterprise WireGuard profile via our company client. nslookup returns timeout. on the bastion `nslookup grafana.internal.redwood` -> 10.4.2.20.

samir: split-tunnel usually only routes private subnets, DNS might be handled by the corporate resolver pushed inside the tunnel. windows DNS client settings can be tricky. quick workaround: ssh local port forward to bastion and forward 3000 -> 10.4.2.20:3000. `ssh -L 3000:10.4.2.20:3000 azureuser@bastion.redwood -N` then browse http://localhost:3000.

noah: that works. thanks. is there a fix so i don't need the tunnel every time?

mira: we'll open a network ticket to add the internal domains to the client split-DNS settings. netops also needs to confirm the WG profile pushes the internal resolver (10.4.0.2). in the meantime, two options: 1) add a persistent SSH config entry so the tunnel is one command, or 2) on Windows, you can add a hosts file entry (c:\windows\system32\drivers\etc\hosts) -> but that won't help TLS certs.

samir: if you're doing lots of browser auth flows (SSO), the hosts hack is painful. also note Windows has a DNS cache; run `ipconfig /flushdns` after editing hosts.

mira: created ticket #6082 to add grafana.internal.redwood to split-DNS and verify resolver push for WireGuard profiles. assigned to @netops. ETA 1 business day.

it-bot: ticket #6082 created: "Add grafana.internal.redwood to VPN split-DNS + resolver push" assigned to netops.

noah: awesome. small follow-up: for folks on macOS, is there anything different? i'm pairing with someone on a Mac and they also hit this.

samir: on macs the network service order and scutil settings determine resolver behavior. often the built-in WireGuard profile will create a new resolver entry automatically; if it doesn't, run `scutil --dns` to inspect. macOS also honors /etc/hosts, but same TLS caveats.

mira: thanks for the heads up. i'll add a short note to the new-hire VPN doc summarizing: 1) how to do an ssh -L tunnel, 2) hosts file caveat and cert issues, 3) macOS scutil command, and 4) who to ping (netops) and the ticket link.

noah: perfect, that would have saved me an hour. thanks y'all :slightly_smiling_face:

netops-bot: noted. will triage #6082 and update this thread when resolved.

it-bot: created onboarding checklist item: "document split-DNS tunnel workaround" assigned to @mira.
